page.description: NomadBSD editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A persistent live FreeBSD system designed to run entirely from a USB flash drive with automatic hardware detection — no ISO, raw disk image only.
pros: SHA-256 checksums published per image via sidecar files
No installation needed — run directly from USB
cons: Media ships as .img.lzma, which ROMinit does not pin
No ISO at all — tools that expect ISO files do not apply
Release from July 2024 (over two years old)
4.7 GiB uncompressed requires at least a 5 GB USB drive
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for NomadBSD; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Decompress with xzcat then write the raw .img to USB with dd; writing erases the whole device. The USB is the system — no install step.
